newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian capital tense as rumours swirl.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian capital tense as rumours swirl.

text.p: The Cambodian capital was tense on Saturday amid fresh rumours of a clash between troops loyal to the two rival prime ministers who are both out of the country.
Soldiers appeared to be on alert across the city but life continued as normal.
Some diplomats however had been advised by a local official to consider moving their families out of the city, one envoy said.
Military officials could not confirm the rumours of a fresh clash. Troops loyal to joint prime ministers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen fought a brief gun battle north of the city on Wednesday.
Both prime ministers were out of the country on Saturday, their offices said.
Witnesses reported seeing small troop units moving in different parts of the city as well as some armoured cars stationed near intersections but said there was nothing out of the ordinary.
Political tension has been high in the capital since Hun Sen warned earlier this week he would use force if he found Ranariddh's military men bringing troops into Phnom Penh illegally.
Ranariddh denied he was moving troops into the city.
Security men loyal to the two prime ministers fought a gun battle in central Phnom Penh on June 17. Two of Ranariddh's bodyguards were killed.
